title: AtlasLane — retail pilot outbound angles & objection map
content:
Context and quick hypothesis:
- Prospect: AtlasLane (regional retail chain, 38 stores, strong loyalty program, mobile-first).
- Why them: consistent transaction volumes, investing in mobile UX, customer service throughput pain during promos, decent engineering org (in-house mobile/web + small data infra team).
- Hypothesis: AtlasLane sees a 10–18% CS ticket surge during weekly promotions and would value automated conversational routing + contextualized product guidance. Pilot scope = checkout-help + returns triage for online orders (mobile app).

Notes/Account background (raw):
- HQ: Midwest; CIO is ex-ecomm startup CTO (likely pragmatic about OSS & hybrid infra).
- Recent headlines: raised strategic capital Q3 2025 for digital experience; posted jobs for "mobile eng lead" and "platform ML".
- Tech stack guesses: React Native mobile, GCP, BigQuery for analytics; uses Zendesk for support (ticketing).
- Security/compliance: processes PII carefully; likely moderate enterprise security requirements (SAML, vendor risk assessments).

Primary personas to target:
- Head of Digital/Product (decision influencer) — cares about conversion and NPS
- Director of Customer Experience (day-to-day owner) — cares about ticket volumes, TTR
- Platform/ML engineer (technical champion) — cares about integration surface, latency, cost
- Legal/Security (procurement blocker) — cares about data residency and logs

Value props we should lead with (short):
- Reduction in ticket volume via prefix-aware LLM routing + quick KB answers (benchmarked 25–40% in similar promos).
- Predictable inference economics via Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) vs unknown cloud API costs — appeal to finance.
- Safe fallbacks: automatic routing to human agents with conversation context + audit logs (for compliance).
- Fast pilot: 4–6 week boxed pilot using Redwood Hosted API, then option to flip to Dedicated or Private if they need isolation.

Pilot scope idea (MVP):
1) Integrate Redwood chat endpoint with Zendesk web widget (orders domain only).
2) Provide 3 canonical flows: order status, returns eligibility, promo stacking rules.
3) Measure: deflection rate, time-to-resolution, fallback rate to human, token cost per session.

Technical constraints / integration risks (to call out proactively):
- Latency SLOs: mobile UX requires <400ms median for quick suggestions — need to configure batching and shorter context windows.
- Regulatory: if they insist on no third-party PII upload, need Private deployment (longer sales cycle).
- KB freshness: product catalog updates hourly during promos — plan to pull deltas into prefix cache or embeddings store with 5–10 minute TTL.
- Zendesk integration complexity: mapping intents to macros, potential need for webhook middleware; include quick Node/Python lambda example.

Outbound approach & sequence (play draft):
- Touch 1 (email): 2–3 sentence value prop + one metric ("pilot that cut promo-support volume by 28% in 6 weeks"). CTA: 20-minute sync to review promo-week runbook.
- Touch 2 (LinkedIn): short note referencing job posting + ask to intro to CX lead.
- Touch 3 (email): lightning demo invite (15 min) + proposed pilot timeline.
- SDR play: route positive replies to AE; use technical discovery checklist before demo (see below).

Discovery checklist (for AE/SE):
- Current ticket volumes by category during peak vs baseline
- Existing bot/FAQ coverage and current deflection rates
- Where knowledge lives (CMS, product DB, Notion) + access cadence
- Latency tolerance per endpoint and fallback workflow
- Procurement timeline, security questionnaire owners

Objection map (raw brainstorm — "objection springs"):
1) "We can't send PII to a 3rd party": Response lines — offer Private deployment or Dedicated inside their VPC; mention encryption at rest and KMS support; propose a short security review workshop.
2) "LLMs hallucinate / produce wrong info": Response lines — show structured output with KB grounding, automated citation snippets, confidence threshold gating, AND can run a human-in-the-loop fallback for low-confidence responses.
3) "Too risky during promotions (high urgency)": Response lines — start with a read-only FAQ assistant that suggests agent macros (no downstream changes), run parallel shadow testing, ramp only when deflection matches safety thresholds.
4) "Cost unpredictability": Response lines — present Dedicated pricing model and Optimize play (quantization + batching) to cap per-token costs; include a sample cost projection for their avg session length.
5) "Implementation effort / internal bandwidth": Response lines — offer a white-glove pilot (SE + solutions engineer), provide prebuilt Zendesk connector and short snippet to spin up in <2 days.

Sample cold/opening lines (brief experiment variants):
- Subject: Quick pilot to cut promo support load by ~25%
- Opening: "Noticed AtlasLane is hiring for mobile and platform ML — congrats. We helped a similarly-sized chain cut promo-week tickets ~28% in 6 weeks with a lightweight Zendesk + LLM pilot. Interested in a 20-min plan?"
- Short alternative (less hype): "Curious how AtlasLane plans to handle support volume during Black Friday — got a 15-minute pilot recipe that might help."

Metrics to prepare for pilot POC deck:
- Baseline ticket counts (orders/returns) + target deflection %
- Expected resolution time improvement and CSAT lift estimate
- Token cost per session estimate (hosted vs dedicated) + projected monthly cost at 10k sessions/mo
- Safety/fallback KPIs: hallucination rate, fallback %

Open questions / TODOs (next actions):
- [ ] Confirm org chart contact for CX and platform (Maya to check LinkedIn connections).
- [ ] Draft short pilot one-pager (SE template) tailored to promos + mobile widget flows (deadline: 2026-01-22).
- [ ] Prepare cost mock for Hosted vs Dedicated for average session lengths (Sandeep).
- [ ] Create demo recording of product answering 10 common promo questions (use synthetic data).
- [ ] Run security bulleted checklist and sample answers for procurement (Ethan).

Quick meeting prep notes (if we get 20-min):
- 0-3m: Why now — promo pain + quick wins
- 3-8m: Our pilot approach and what we need from them (data, widget access)
- 8-14m: Demo + expected results + safety model
- 14-20m: Next steps and ask (commit to a 4–6 week pilot + pilot owner)

Random scratch thoughts (brain-dump):
- Could propose a co-branded "help assistant" that surfaces loyalty info — could be a wedge into personalization team.
- If they push back on PII, explore token-filtering on client side (hashing order numbers) to reduce concerns.
- Keep pitch modular: start with read-only answer bot -> escalate to order-lookup capabilities -> then returns processing automation.

If we get a greenlight: founder-level email cadence + SE intro + contract SOW template (I have a draft SOW in the playbook link above).

-- end scratch journal --

Notes-to-self: keep this lightweight, expect many back-and-forths; capture their "must have" compliance items early to avoid surprises.
